transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I guess I'm here because the clinic doctor got on my case about my eating. I mean, most days I just keep it simple. I'll have coffee in the morning, maybe grab a few bites of something between painting jobs... and then just a small dinner, assuming I'm not too busy catching up on my class paperwork. It's just what works for my schedule.
When you eat very little, do you worry about gaining weight or becoming heavier?

Yeah, I do. If I eat something heavy, like a big sandwich or pizza, I get this panicky feeling. I start worrying that I'll just wake up bigger and slower. With painting and papering, I'm up and down ladders all day, moving around rooms and equipment... I need to be light on my feet. I just worry I won't be able to move around the way I need to for my job if I put on weight.
Has your weight become significantly low for your height and age?

Well, my work pants are definitely hanging pretty loose on me lately. And, um, people on the job sites keep making comments, telling me I look too thin. But honestly, I just see it as having leaned out from being on my feet all day. I'm constantly moving.
Has a doctor told you that your current weight is significantly below what is healthy for your height?

Yeah, the clinic doctor did say it was way below where it should be. But... I don't really think my weight is some kind of emergency, even though everyone keeps acting like it is. Honestly, to me, it just feels like they're making a huge deal out of me being disciplined and staying busy with my work. I just don't see the problem.
